title: Additive comparison for the strict Roos cone
statement:
Let A and B be abelian categories with countable products and F : A to B an additive functor. Suppose the canonical product comparison is invertible for every strict tower complex. Then F commutes with the actual shifted Roos mapping cones by an isomorphism with the stated canonical biproduct/product coordinates, natural for strict tower maps and commuting with positive arithmetic restriction maps given by block and selection. No scalar-extension assertion or quasi-isomorphism assertion is included.

theorem strictRoosAdditiveComparison
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [Category.{vA} A] [Category.{vB} B]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [HasCountableProducts A] [HasCountableProducts B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (hprod : ∀ X : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ,
      IsIso (piComparison (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.asFunctor.obj (op n)))) :
      ∃ θ : ∀ X : CochainComplex
          (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ,
          (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (strictRoosComplex X) ≅
            strictRoosComplex
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X),
        (∀ X (p : ℤ), (θ X).hom.f (p + 1) ≫
            (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X) p).hom =
          F.map (strictRoosCoordinates X p).hom ≫
            F.biprodComparison ((strictRoosProduct X).X p)
              ((strictRoosProduct X).X (p + 1)) ≫
            biprod.map ((piComparison (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
              (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.asFunctor.obj (op n))).f p)
              ((piComparison (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
              (fun n : ℕ ↦ X.asFunctor.obj (op n))).f (p + 1))) ∧
        (∀ X Y (f : X ⟶ Y),
          ∃ (μ : strictRoosComplex X ⟶ strictRoosComplex Y)
            (ν : strictRoosComplex
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X) ⟶
              strictRoosComplex
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Y)),
          (∀ p : ℤ, μ.f (p + 1) ≫ (strictRoosCoordinates Y p).hom =
            (strictRoosCoordinates X p).hom ≫
              biprod.map ((strictRoosProductMap f).f p)
                ((strictRoosProductMap f).f (p + 1))) ∧
          (∀ p : ℤ, ν.f (p + 1) ≫
              (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Y) p).hom =
            (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X) p).hom ≫
              biprod.map ((strictRoosProductMap
                  ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)).f p)
                ((strictRoosProductMap
                  ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)).f (p + 1))) ∧
          (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map μ ≫ (θ Y).hom = (θ X).hom ≫ ν) ∧
        (∀ X (e : ℕ) (_he : 1 ≤ e),
          ∃ (ρ : strictRoosComplex X ⟶ strictRoosComplex
              ((complexRestriction (A) e).obj X))
            (ρB : strictRoosComplex
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X) ⟶
              strictRoosComplex
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
                ((complexRestriction (A) e).obj X))),
          (∀ p : ℤ, ρ.f (p + 1) ≫ (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((complexRestriction (A) e).obj X) p).hom =
            (strictRoosCoordinates X p).hom ≫
              biprod.map ((block e X.asFunctor).f p)
                ((selection e X.asFunctor).f (p + 1))) ∧
          (∀ p : ℤ, ρB.f (p + 1) ≫ (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
              ((complexRestriction (A) e).obj X)) p).hom =
            (strictRoosCoordinates
              ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X) p).hom ≫
              biprod.map ((block e ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X).asFunctor).f p)
                ((selection e ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj X).asFunctor).f (p + 1))) ∧
          (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map ρ ≫
              (θ ((complexRestriction (A) e).obj X)).hom =
            (θ X).hom ≫ ρB)

proof.text: Construct the product comparison and show by each product projection that it intertwines 1-s. Apply the additive cone isomorphism, the isomorphism of product arrows and the shift comparison to construct theta. Compute the two coordinates using XIsoOfEq naturality, the cone coordinate formula and biproduct projections. A general square of product arrows gives a square of these cone maps, checked coordinatewise. For strict maps, product naturality supplies that square. For arithmetic restriction, sum_range_sub telescopes the block differential; selection and the finite block sums commute with the canonical product comparison by projection extensionality and additivity. Apply the same cone-map square. All assertions, including theta naturality and the arithmetic square, are proved in Lean without new holes.
